Dunaivtsi Old Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Khmelnytskyi Oblast, Ukraine

Demolished. Dunaivtsi's Jewish community was destroyed twice — during the Khmelnytsky massacre of 1648–49 and again during the Haidamak rebellions of the 1760s — and suffered a blood libel accusation in 1748. By 1910, the population had peaked at 9,221 (70.7 percent of the town), supported by eleven synagogues and two printing houses. During the WWII occupation, more than 7,000 people were executed or buried alive in the Solonich forest, and approximately 12,000 Jews were murdered in the town in total — one of the largest death tolls documented in this collection. This is the older of Dunaivtsi's two Jewish cemeteries; in 1871–72, the Jewish community purchased a plot specifically for a Jewish cemetery.
